channel.title: Harikesh Mishra
channel.description: Long-form guides on how JavaScript and React actually work, by Harikesh Mishra.

item.title: Processes, Threads, and How Servers Handle Work
item.description: From programs on disk to processes, CPU scheduling, context switches, and threads, with the connection to Node.js and libuv.

item.title: Node.js Runtime and the V8 Engine
item.description: How Node.js extends JavaScript, how V8 executes and optimizes code, and how the engine manages memory.

item.title: React Data Fetching and Server State
item.description: A guide to remote data as a cache: query keys, stale data, mutations, optimistic updates, and Suspense.

item.title: React Error Boundaries and Resilience
item.description: What React catches, how it recovers, and how error boundaries contain failures in real applications.

item.title: React's Event System
item.description: How synthetic events, delegation, propagation, portals, and event priority work in modern React.

item.title: React Hooks and Effects
item.description: A practical mental model for hooks, renders, effects, closures, and React's update queues.

item.title: React Performance Architecture
item.description: A measured approach to rendering cost, memoization, concurrency, virtualization, and bundle size.

item.title: React Rendering and Reconciliation Internals
item.description: A guided deep dive into how React turns state into UI, compares trees, and keeps updates responsive.

item.title: React's Scheduler and Lanes
item.description: A guided tour of cooperative scheduling, update priority, lanes, and React's concurrent work loop.

item.title: React Server Components and the Server/Client Boundary
item.description: A clear model of Server Components, Client Components, serialization, streaming, and framework boundaries.

item.title: React State Management Architecture
item.description: How to choose where state lives, avoid contradictions, and scale shared state without unnecessary complexity.

item.title: React Suspense Internals
item.description: How promises suspend rendering, boundaries reveal content, retries work, and transitions prevent jarring fallbacks.

item.title: JavaScript Type Conversion: Why '6' / '2' Is 3
item.description: How JavaScript converts values to strings, numbers, and booleans, including coercion, NaN, truthy and falsy values, and the special behavior of plus.

item.title: setTimeout, Closures, and the Famous Loop Problem
item.description: Why delayed callbacks share one var binding, how let creates a binding per loop iteration, and how helper functions preserve each value.

item.title: JavaScript Scope: How Names Find Their Values
item.description: How global, function, and block scope shape name lookup, lexical environments, scope chains, hoisting, shadowing, and ReferenceError behavior.

item.title: var, let, and const: Bindings, Scope, and the TDZ
item.description: Compare var, let, and const through declaration setup, scope, redeclaration, reassignment, global behavior, and the Temporal Dead Zone.

item.title: JavaScript Blocks, Scope, and Shadowing
item.description: How blocks group statements, how let and const create block scope, how shadowing works, and why some redeclarations are illegal.

item.title: Map, Filter, and Reduce: Transform, Select, Combine
item.description: Learn how map, filter, and reduce work through numbers, user records, accumulator traces, and practical combinations.

item.title: How JavaScript Keeps Track of Running Code
item.description: Understand execution contexts, the call stack, and how asynchronous code fits into JavaScript's single-threaded execution model.

item.title: JavaScript Hoisting Does Not Move Your Code
item.description: What actually happens to var, let, const, function, class, and function-expression bindings before JavaScript evaluates a scope.

item.title: Higher-Order Functions: Stop Rewriting the Loop
item.description: How passing and returning functions separates repeated control flow from changing logic, with a circle calculator built step by step.

item.title: Global Scope and this: Look at the Call Site
item.description: How global bindings, classic scripts, modules, strict mode, methods, arrows, constructors, and event listeners determine the value of this.

item.title: JavaScript Functions Are Values with Behavior
item.description: A practical tour of declarations, expressions, names, parameters, returned functions, first-class behavior, and arrow functions.

item.title: JavaScript Concurrency: One Thread, Many Tasks
item.description: How JavaScript makes progress on timers, network requests, rendering, and user input without confusing concurrency with parallel execution.

item.title: Callback Hell: When JavaScript Starts Leaning Sideways
item.description: How dependent asynchronous callbacks create the pyramid of doom, scatter errors, surrender control, and how promises and async functions restore structure.

item.title: Callback Functions: JavaScript Calls You Back
item.description: What callbacks really are, when they run synchronously or asynchronously, and how they shape timers, events, array methods, and closures.

item.title: JavaScript, the Browser, and the Event Loop
item.description: How browser APIs, tasks, microtasks, and the event loop let JavaScript handle delayed work without blocking the main thread.

item.title: More on Closures: Scope Chains, Privacy, and Memory
item.description: A deeper look at returned functions, lexical bindings, shadowing, private state, constructor closures, and garbage collection.

item.title: setTimeout Has Trust Issues
item.description: Why a timer delay is a minimum, not an exact execution time, explained through the call stack and event loop.

item.title: How the JavaScript Engine Runs Your Code
item.description: From source text to bytecode and optimized machine code, with the runtime, call stack, heap, and garbage collector explained.

item.title: Closures in JavaScript: The Function's Backpack
item.description: How functions remember lexical scope, retain changing bindings, and use that memory for counters, currying, memoization, and async code.
